title: Module 6 · Lesson 1 — The production RAG pipeline stage by stage

lines: This lesson walks the production RAG pipeline, stage by stage.
Most hallucination complaints are really retrieval failures.

say.0: This lesson walks the production rag pipeline, stage by stage.

lines: Picture a solar company whose assistant helps technicians read installation manuals.
Up on a roof, a technician asks for a clamp's torque setting.
The assistant confidently gives the wrong number.
A bigger model won't help: the spec was lost before the model saw it.
The pipeline has seven stages: extract, chunk, embed, index, retrieve, rerank, and generate.
Each one fails in its own recognizable way.
Extraction is where most quality is lost: the torque table became a run-on line of numbers.
Table-aware parsing, like NeMo Retriever extraction, keeps each value under its header.

say.1: Table-aware parsing, like Nemo Retriever extraction, keeps each value under its header.

lines: Chunking should follow headings, sections, and tables, with a small overlap.
Every chunk carries metadata: source, section, date, access level, and version.
Chunks too small lose their context; too large, and the embedding blurs.
Small-to-big searches small chunks, but returns the whole parent section.
Question-answer embedders encode questions and passages differently.
Encode a query as if it were a passage, and recall silently drops.
Changing the embedding model means re-embedding everything.
Vectors from two different models simply can't be compared.
Vector search misses exact tokens, like the inverter error code E-42.
Hybrid search adds keyword search, and fuses both lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

say.0: Vector search misses exact tokens, like the inverter error code E forty-two.

lines: Metadata filters run before the vector search, so restricted manuals are never candidates.
Filtering afterwards leaks what exists and wastes recall.
A cross-encoder reranker is accurate, but too slow for a whole corpus.
So retrieve the top fifty cheaply, then rerank down to the best three to five.
Finally, the prompt says: answer only from the sources, and cite every claim.
If they don't cover it, say so instead of guessing.
The trap: a reranker only reorders what retrieval returned, so it can't rescue a missing document.
Fix recall upstream, with hybrid search, better chunking, or query rewriting.
On the exam, wrong table numbers mean extraction, and missed codes mean hybrid search.
Read on for each stage in detail.
